name: Multa Lakes
full: Multa Lakes — a cascade of glacial lakes in the Multa river valley on the northern slope of the Katun Range: Lower (1,710 m), Middle (1,740–1,860 m), Upper (1,920 m), as well as Poperechnoye, Kuiguk, Akchan and others; start points — the villages of Multa/Zamulta and Maralnik-1
near: Maralnik-1 (≈12–13 km to the Lower Lake), Multa and Zamulta (≈20–22 km); the district centre Ust-Koksa ≈30–43 km
elev: Lower 1,710 m; Middle 1,740 m (1,860 m per tonkosti); Upper 1,920 m (zapovedtravel ~1,860 m); the whole cascade 1,700–2,030 m
short: A necklace of turquoise glacial lakes under the Katun Range, linked by the roaring “Shumy” rapids — one of the most beautiful and most visited places in the Ust-Koksa district.
desc: The Multa river flows out of a cascade of glacial lakes on the northern slope of the Katun Range. Lower Multa Lake (1,710 m) is the largest: ~2.37×0.7–1 km, up to 20–21 m deep, warming up to +15 °C in summer, with huge moraine boulders along the southern shore and pebble beaches along the northern one. Between the Lower and Middle lakes is the “Shumy” rapids-waterfall (a drop of ~30 m). The Middle Lake (~2×0.6 km, up to 20 m) is already on the edge of the Katun Biosphere Reserve. The Upper Lake (1,920 m, 1.4×0.4 km, 47.7 m deep, water up to +10 °C) lies in a cirque with waterfalls of 47–60 m, entirely inside the reserve, and requires a permit. In the neighbouring valleys are Poperechnoye, Kuiguk and Akchan; through the Kuiguk Pass (1A, 2,520 m) loop routes lead to Kyrgyz Lake and Tyungur. To the Lower Lake from Maralnik-1 it is 12–13 km along a rutted forest road: 4–6 h on foot or 1.5–3 h in a GAZ-66; passenger cars cannot go beyond Maralnik. At the Lower Lake the mountain complex of the “Multa Lakes” tourist complex operates (cabins, glamping), with boats on the Lower and Middle lakes. The season is late June to mid-September; in winter there are snowmobile tours. There is no phone coverage at the lakes.
guide: Do not stop at the Lower Lake, where the bases are: walk or take a boat to the “Shumy” and the Middle Lake — there the scene is completely different and wild. If you have the energy for a second day, arrange a permit and climb to the Upper Lake: the deepest (almost 48 m) and coldest lake of the cascade, with waterfalls in the cirque. Locals call the road from Maralnik “mud porridge” — if you walk, wet feet are guaranteed, and in a GAZ-66 hold on tight. Be sure to download offline maps: navigation apps suggest a non-existent road via Inegen and Tyungur.
see: The Lower Multa Lake (beaches, boulders, boat); the “Shumy” waterfall-rapids; the Middle Multa Lake; the Upper Multa Lake with waterfalls of 47–60 m (reserve); Poperechnoye Lake; Kuiguk and the Kuiguk Pass; forest and berry patches along the Multa valley.
skip: you do not have 2–3 days for this area alone: the road from Gorno-Altaysk is 6–8 h one way plus 1.5–6 h of transfer — too much for a couple of hours at the lake; and if you are not ready for mud, cold and no phone coverage.
diff: Moderate: 12–13 km on foot to the Lower Lake with constant climbing (4–6 h, mud); to the Upper Lake — another ~7 km from the Middle Lake (~2 h one way). With a GAZ-66 transfer — easy but bumpy. The loop via Kuiguk is difficult (1A pass).
when: Late June to early/mid-September (best from July to mid-August); in June — flowers and full waterfalls, but snow at the upper lakes; frosts from September; in winter — snowmobile tours.
hours: A natural area; the permit for the Katun Reserve (for the Upper Lake) is available at the office in Ust-Koksa (Mon–Fri 8:00–16:00) or at the ranger post by the Middle Lake; entry to the reserve is only in daylight (tonkosti/zapovedtravel data).
daytime: Morning — calm water and reflections on the Lower Lake (editorial).
how: Gorno-Altaysk — Ust-Koksa via the Chuysky Trakt and through Ust-Kan/Tuekta: ~320–424 km, 6–8 h (paved, mostly gravel after Ust-Koksa). Then Ust-Koksa — Multa/Zamulta — Maralnik-1 (~43 km from Ust-Koksa to Maralnik per Wikipedia). From Maralnik-1 (or Multa) to the Lower Lake it is 12–22 km only on foot, on horseback or by GAZ-66/UAZ. Navigation apps suggest a non-existent road via Inegen and Tyungur. From Novosibirsk ~830 km, Barnaul ~550, Biysk ~380 km. Buses run daily from Gorno-Altaysk and Barnaul to Ust-Koksa (8–10 h), then a taxi/base transfer.
needcar: Yes: to Multa/Maralnik — your own car, or a bus to Ust-Koksa + taxi; to the lakes — GAZ-66/UAZ, horse or on foot.
self: Yes: on foot along the beaten road/path from Maralnik-1 (there are forks — an offline map is needed) or with a transfer by locals. For the Upper Lake — get a reserve permit.
roadtype: Paved up to Ust-Koksa; Ust-Koksa — Multa — Maralnik: gravel/dirt, a passenger car can reach Maralnik-1; beyond that — a rutted muddy forest road only for GAZ-66/UAZ, with stretches of wooden decking towards the Upper Lake.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Multa 6–8 h (1–2 days from Novosibirsk); transfer 1.5–3 h; on foot 4–6 h to the Lower Lake; Middle — Upper ~2 h.
stay: “Multa Lakes” tourist complex (Zamulta, 4 Novaya St., +7 909 508-10-77): rooms 3,500–8,000 ₽, economy 3,500–5,500 ₽, tent 500 ₽; the mountain complex at the Lower Lake — cabins 4,000 ₽ per person, glamping sphere 12,000 ₽, chalets 12,000–15,000 ₽ (2026). Kedrovaya Opushka base (Maralnik-1, 9 Gornaya St., +7 909 508-25-38): cabins from 1,200 ₽, tent from 400 ₽ (year not stated). At the reserve ranger post by the Upper Lake there is a hut for up to 10 people. All campsites at the Multa Lakes are paid (sport-marafon).
net: There is no phone coverage or internet at the lakes (zapovedtravel, kp.ru); in Multa/Ust-Koksa there is (operators not specified).
entry: Permit for the Katun Reserve (Upper Lake) — 200 ₽ per person per day (turistka.ru 2026, seven.travel); campsites by the lakes are paid (tent 400–500 ₽). Whether the Lower/Middle Lake falls under the paid regional protected areas (300 ₽ from 01.07.2026) — not found. No resort fee.
transfer: GAZ-66 to the Lower Lake 3,000–4,000 ₽ per person (2026); older sources say 2,500 ₽ (kp.ru).
bring: Warm waterproof clothing, trekking boots (mud), sun protection, offline maps (the “Karta RU” app), passport for the permit, cash (ATM — Ust-Koksa), tick and mosquito repellent, a gas stove.
warn: No phone coverage. The road from Maralnik is mud and ruts. To the Upper Lake — only with a Katun Reserve permit and in daylight. Navigation apps lead you along the non-existent Inegen — Tyungur road. Border zone: the Ust-Koksa district is partly in the border zone (the Karagaiskoye, Amurskoye, Ust-Koksinskoye, Ognevskoye, Katandinskoye, Taldinskoye and Verkh-Uimonskoye settlements); the Multa Lakes are not on the list — Russian citizens need only a passport; foreigners should check with the FSB border directorate (on the way through Ust-Koksa). Ticks and bears (in 2026 — attacks in Altai). Night frosts at the lakes are possible even in summer.
food: Meals at the tourist complex and the mountain complex; in the Uimon valley — Old Believer dishes (honey, mead, pelmeni), Altai kai-chai (cafe names not found).
reviews: Aggregated 2GIS/Yandex ratings not found. Typical pros — “one of the 10 most beautiful places in Russia”, turquoise water, Shumy; cons — a hard muddy road, paid campsites, crowded at the Lower Lake in July–August.

p.sum: A long but rewarding trip: 6–8 h from Gorno-Altaysk to Multa/Maralnik-1, then 12–22 km to the Lower Lake on foot or by GAZ-66 (3,000–4,000 ₽). Stay at the mountain complex by the Lower Lake or in Zamulta; on the second day — Shumy, the Middle and Upper lakes (reserve permit 200 ₽).

p.permits: Katun Reserve permit for the Upper Lake (200 ₽/day; office in Ust-Koksa, 1 Zapovednaya St., Mon–Fri 8–16, or the ranger post by the Middle Lake; passport). A border-zone permit is not needed for Russian citizens (the lakes are outside the list); foreigners should check with the FSB border directorate for the Altai Republic. For hiking groups — online registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS).
p.access: Children — with a GAZ-66 transfer (bumpy); hard for older people; dogs in the reserve — not found (usually prohibited).
